messages:
anika: Quick update — finished the small-sweep bring-up for model v3.2-qf (light quant + frozen KV). Results below, proposing a stability-window gating rule before wider promotion.
sean: awesome, can you paste the key numbers?
anika: yes — A/B (baseline v3.1 vs candidate v3.2-qf) over 1.2k sampled requests: 
```
latency_p50_ms: 98 -> 112 (+14)
latency_p95_ms: 210 -> 260 (+50)
cmp_accuracy: 0.872 -> 0.864 (-0.009)
hallucination_rate: 3.1% -> 3.6% (+0.5pp)
token_cost_usd_per_1k: 0.72 -> 0.51 (-29%)
```
(seems like latency regressed a bit, quality small delta, cost looks good)
maria: thanks. is that with continuous batching on? and what batch sizes?
anika: yes, runtime batching on. Sweep tried batch_size [1,4,8], typical traffic skewed to 1 and 4. The latency hit concentrated at colder requests with long contexts where KV is frozen.
kevin: interesting — what's your confidence envelope? are those deltas stable across two independent runs?
anika: ran 3 independent micro-burns over different hours — deltas consistent within ±0.004 on cmp_accuracy, latency variance larger during peak. I pushed full logs to the eval dash link: https://redwood.internal/evals/2026/2109-v3-2-qf
eva: can we validate semantic regressions with the targeted prompt set? last time small accuracy diffs hid high-impact failures.
anika: ran the targeted suite (200 prompts): 6 critical-level regressions flagged (same user-impact categories as last rollout). Manual review attached in the drive doc.
deploy-bot: canary: rollout started for v3.2-qf -> 1% traffic (policy: sticky by user, shadow warmup 15m).
sean: given the cost win but sighted quality regressions, what's the gating proposal?
anika: propose a 3-tier gate: 1) smoke (0-1%): no critical regressions in targeted suite, 2) stability-window (1-10% over 24h): rolling metric checks every hour comparing last 1k requests, 3) soft-promotion to 50% only if stability window shows cmp_accuracy delta >= -0.005 and hallucination delta <= +0.2pp and latency_p95 delta <= +35ms. If any check fails for two consecutive hours -> automatic fallback to previous stable model.\maria: can we tighten the automatic fallback to trigger on a single hour if critical regression count > 0?
anika: yes, we'll make critical-regressions immediate-fallback. Config snippet: 
```
rollout_policy:
  phases:
    - name: smoke
      traffic: 1%
      checks: [smoke-suite-no-critical]
    - name: stability-window
      traffic: 1-10%
      window: 24h
      compare_last_n: 1000
      thresholds:
        cmp_accuracy_delta: -0.005
        hallucination_pp_delta: 0.2
        latency_p95_ms_delta: 35
      fallback_on: [threshold_exceed, critical_regression]
    - name: soft-promo
      traffic: 50%
      checks: [rolling-eval, anomaly-detection]
  automatic_fallback: true
```
kevin: that looks reasonable. Suggest add an early-noise-floor to prevent flip-flopping on tiny deltas: require delta to exceed metric_noise_floor for two consecutive windows.
eva: agree — also annotate user cohorts to avoid promoting when a single cohort gets all the bad traffic (we saw rollout skew last time).
anika: will add cohort-breakdown and noise-floor (currently noise_floor_cmp_accuracy: 0.002). Also will enable a 2-hour cooldown after any auto-fallback.
sean: what's the manual override path? ops should be able to pause or pin via the console.
anika: yes, we added console actions: pause-rollout, pin-previous, force-promote (requires 2 approvers).
eva: for rollout telemetry, please add per-route latency p95 and 99, hallucination by intent bucket, and sample-level golden prompts attached to every check failure.
anika: noted. I'll update the policy and re-run another 2k request smoke in morning. plan: tighten thresholds, push updated policy by 11:00 PST, then run extended 5% burn for 6h if green.
maria: sounds good. thanks. :thumbsup:
eval-bot: eval: targeted-suite completed, 0 critical in latest run (post-policy-tweak), flagged 2 medium regressions (refer to report).
sean: ok let's let the 6h burn run. keep Slack pings to @eng-oncall if anything trips.
anika: will do — I'll post a short summary at end of burn and open a follow-up thread with the final A/B table.
